origin_result.basis: Final manufacture did not take place in the UAE. The operations performed are all minimal operations under Article 3.5.1 (changes of packaging, simple packaging, affixing marks). One non-originating input is in the same heading 8504 as the product, representing 88.0% of the price, above the 10% de minimis. Value addition is only 12.0% against a required 40% on an FOB basis.

caveats.note: A lower 15% rate under Notification 45/2025-Customs applies only for electric-vehicle manufacture; Mansha uses the general 20% rate.
Mansha has not checked whether India charges anti-dumping duty on this product; check with Indian customs or a customs broker.
The '+' in the rule is interpreted as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+'.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ from the estimate.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only; IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically; the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, which is required before applying for the certificate of origin for India.
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is unconfirmed.

gaps: Mansha has not checked whether India charges anti-dumping duty on battery chargers.
